title: How to Use Tax-Loss Harvesting to Improve Retirement Returns
description: Turning market losses into a government subsidy for your portfolio.
content:
No one likes losing money. But in a taxable brokerage account, a loss is a valuable asset. **Tax-Loss Harvesting (TLH)** is the practice of selling an investment that is down, banking the 'loss' for tax purposes, and immediately buying a similar investment to stay in the market. This creates a 'Tax Asset' you can use to offset future gains or ordinary income. Over a 20-year period, consistent TLH can add 0.50% to 1.00% to your annual after-tax returns, essentially letting the IRS subsidize your bear markets.

Key Takeaways

  • The $3,000 Income Deduction: You can use net losses to offset up to $3,000 of ordinary income (wages) per year. This saves you ~$1,000 in cash taxes annually.
  • Unlimited Offset: You can use losses to offset unlimited capital gains. If you sell a house for a $100k profit, you can use $100k of harvested stock losses to pay $0 tax.
  • The Wash Sale Rule: You cannot sell a stock and buy the 'substantially identical' stock within 30 days. You must swap to a similar but different ETF (e.g., VTI to SCHB).
  • Deferral, Not Avoidance: TLH lowers your cost basis, meaning you will pay more tax later when you sell. But delaying taxes for 20 years is a massive win due to the time value of money.

Why It Matters (US Context)

TLH only applies to Taxable Accounts. You cannot harvest losses in an IRA or 401(k). As retirees shift to living off taxable accounts in early retirement, harvesting becomes a key tool to manage AGI and ACA subsidies.

The Harvesting Workflow

Scenario: The market drops 10%.

Step 1: Identify Losers

You bought VOO (S&P 500) for $10,000.
It is now worth $9,000.
Paper Loss: $1,000.

Step 2: The Swap

Sell VOO for $9,000. (Realize the $1,000 loss).
Immediately buy VTI (Total Market) for $9,000.
Result: You are still invested in US stocks. You didn't 'sell low and go to cash'. You stayed in the market.

Step 3: The Tax Benefit

On your tax return, you deduct that $1,000 loss.
If in the 24% bracket, you save $240 in taxes.
You essentially got a 2.4% return on your original $10k just by clicking a few buttons.

Advanced Tactics

  1. Robo-Advisors: Betterment/Wealthfront do this automatically every day. The value of daily harvesting often pays for their 0.25% fee in volatile years.
  2. Donating Low Basis: Years later, you have VTI with a very low cost basis (high potential tax). Donate these shares to charity via a Donor Advised Fund. You get the full deduction and never pay the tax. It washes away the liability.
  3. Specific ID: When you sell, always tell your broker to use 'Specific ID' cost basis. Sell the shares with the losses, keep the shares with the gains.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it legal?

Yes, it is explicitly allowed by the IRS as long as you avoid the Wash Sale rule (buying the exact same thing back). VOO and VTI are different indices, so they are generally considered safe swaps.

Does it work in an IRA?

No. Losses in an IRA are not deductible. This is a strategy exclusively for your Brokerage account.

What if I buy it back in 31 days?

That's fine. The Wash Sale window is 30 days. After that, you can buy back the original ticker if you really prefer it.
